prompt: We have a marketing landing page with no build step at all -- just a plain index.html loaded straight in the browser, no bundler, no npm install. I want to show a 'first-time buyer' banner only when three things are all true: the cart total is under $50, the customer's region is one of US/CA/GB, and this is their first purchase. Can you wire this up using verdict-rules loaded from a CDN, and show or hide the #first-time-buyer-banner element based on the result?
expected_output: A <script> tag loading verdict-rules from a CDN (jsDelivr or unpkg), pinned to a specific version with a real integrity attribute (or, if using the ESM +esm CDN path instead, an explicit note that no integrity hash is possible there since it transforms on the fly), building the three-condition rule set with the global VerdictRules API (or an ESM import), and toggling the banner's hidden attribute based on the RuleResult's passed field.
expectations: The script tag loading verdict-rules from a CDN is pinned to a specific version, never an unversioned URL
The script tag carries a real integrity attribute matching the pinned version, OR the response explicitly states why one isn't used if the ESM +esm CDN path is chosen instead
The three conditions (cart total, region, first purchase) are each represented as an independent, named rule -- not one inline boolean expression
The rule-evaluation logic and the DOM update (toggling the banner) are kept as separate concerns, not interleaved inside the same function
The banner's visibility is driven by the RuleResult's passed field, not a re-derived boolean computed separately from the rule evaluation
No bundler, npm install, or build step is introduced -- the solution respects that this page explicitly has none
